Series

by Enrique Metinides; ed. Misha Kominek; text by Véronique Ricardoni

Description

"Series" presents Enrique Metinides' iconic crime and disaster photography through a cinematographic lens, organizing 100 photographs—both color and black & white duotone—across fourteen thematic sequences. The book examines works including "Explosion," "The Tower Suicide," and "The Lovers of Chapultepec," revealing how Metinides captures human reactions to tragedy: the faces and postures of survivors after their lives have been fundamentally altered. The sequential arrangement transforms tabloid images into a compassionate documentation where survivors become the focus rather than sensationalism. Metinides' fifty-year career documenting Mexico City's tragedies reveals the city's juxtaposition of mechanical brutality, opulence, and poverty.

Notes

Text by Véronique Ricardoni (English/Spanish), translated by Shawn Volesky. Recognized by TIME Magazine photo editors, the British Journal of Photography, photo-eye and others as one of the best photobooks of 2011. Enrique Metinides (1934-2022) earned the nickname "El Niño" (The Boy) after publishing his first photograph at age twelve. He worked from 1949 to 1979 as a photographer for La Prensa and other Mexico City tabloids.
